title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 2: Vulgate "conformes fieri" — not election from foresight of works
pass_a_gloss: Secondly, the Apostle did not say, whom he foreknew would be conformed, he predestinated; but, whom he foreknew (that is, foreloved) he predestinated to be made conformed, as the Vulgate version has rightly supplied what is wanting in the Greek context. God therefore is not said to predestinate from the foreknowledge of our works, but to foreknow our good works which he prepared for the predestinated.
pass_b_english: Second: Paul did not write "whom he foreknew would be conformed, he predestined," but "whom he foreknew" (that is, foreloved) "he predestined to become conformed" — as the Vulgate rightly supplies what the Greek leaves open. So God is not said to predestine from foresight of our works, but to foreknow the good works he prepared for those already predestined.
source_text: Secundo, non dixit Apostolus, quos praescivit futuros conformes praedestinavit; sed, quos praescivit (hoc est, predilexit) praedestinavit conformes fieri, ut vulgata versio recte supplevit, quod in Graeco contextu deest. Non itaque Deus praedestinare dicitur ex praescientia operum nostrorum, sed praescire bona nostra opera quae praedestinatis praeparavit.
